title: Multi-centric Validation of the FAST4D Score in Emergency medical service STroke dEtection and Capability to predict large vessel occlusion eligible for endovascular Treatment
summary:
The early detection of a stroke is important in order to initiate time-critical therapy in a suitable clinic. There is a standardized examination procedure established in emergency medicine that is intended to quickly identify patients with a possible stroke. This FAST test includes the English acronyms face, facial asymmetry, arm, one-sided descent when trying to hold the arm, speech, speech and language disorders, and time, which is intended to indicate the urgency of adequate treatment. If you look at the FAST test critically, only symptoms of a stroke in the area supplied by the internal carotid artery are recorded, strictly speaking only those in the area supplied by the middle cerebral artery. Strokes in the area of the Aa. The area supplied by the vertebral and basilar arteries is not well covered.
By expanding the FAST test to include “4D”, where 4D stands for 4 additional English acronyms: Dizziness/Vertigo, Diplopic images, Deficite in the field of view and Dysmetria/ataxia (deficit in the finger-nose test), typical symptoms of a stroke in the vertebrobasilar vascular area are recorded. This simple extension of the FAST test to FAST4D has already led to an improvement in stroke detection by the emergency services in a monocentric observation study in the Lahn-Dill emergency services area.
After the data from the FAST4D study showed that FAST4D detects significantly more patients with stroke, the project planned here must now examine whether better detection of these patients also leads to an improvement in acute medical care. If it can be shown that FAST4D not only detects more patients with stroke but also improves their care, this has implications for future guidelines and recommendations.

interventions.name:
Conservative patients with suspected stroke and referred by the emergency services as well as all patients with a discharge diagnosis of stroke.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients who are referred to the emergency room with suspected stroke in one of the participating clinics. These patients receive a patient allocation code (PZC) from the emergency services, which they use to register electronically at the destination clinic. There are 3 codes for stroke, depending on the onset of symptoms. All patients with these codes are recorded: 421/422/423 (“Apoplexy/TIA/Hemorrhage”)
In order to record patients who are not assigned as having a stroke but were diagnosed with a stroke during diagnostics, all patients with the corresponding discharge diagnosis are also recorded.
For the retrospective control group, the identification of patients is carried out in the same way by screening the patients who were suspected of having a stroke in the emergency room during this time and after the discharge diagnosis. The retrospective data collection will cover the year 2023.
Exclusion criteria:
none
